Container.Name: deepseek-harness
Container.Overview:
DeepSeek Harness (dsh) - browser-based agent runtime from DeepSeek AI, packaged from the official npm release. Official upstream code, unmodified: the container only adds a config layer and one small plugin on top of the published package, so a new upstream release is a rebuild rather than a fork.
PRIVATE IMAGE: Before installing or updating, open the Unraid terminal and run "docker login ghcr.io -u prv-ctech". At Docker's password prompt, paste a GitHub personal access token (classic) with read:packages and access to this package. Do not put the token in this template or a container variable. See the repository README for details.
After registry login, the container needs no appdata setup. It takes ownership of its own appdata at startup, then drops to PUID:PGID before dsh runs. Defaults PUID=99 and PGID=100 match Unraid's usual nobody:users ownership, so a freshly created appdata directory works with no chown from a terminal.
GETTING THE LOGIN URL: dsh requires a launch token and prints the URL to open in its log: [br] docker logs deepseek-harness[br] Look for the line starting "dsh web (proxy):" or "dsh web:". Open that URL once; it exchanges the token for a cookie valid for 30 days. THE TOKEN ROTATES ON EVERY RESTART, so after a container update or restart, re-read the log. Seeing "authentication required" or HTTP 401 means exactly that - it is not a misconfiguration.
BROWSING BY IP OR BY NAME: dsh accepts a request only if the hostname in the address bar is trusted - otherwise the API answers HTTP 403. Non-internal IPv4 addresses are trusted automatically, so http://[IP]:[PORT:3080] works with no configuration. A HOSTNAME (e.g. unraid.local or a domain behind a reverse proxy) must be declared: put it in DSH PUBLIC HOST below, or add it to EXTRA TRUSTED HOSTS to keep several working at once. This is upstream's DNS-rebinding and CSRF protection, and it is what stops a malicious page on your LAN from reaching the API.
TLS AND THE INTERNET: dsh serves plain HTTP and sends no security headers. Unraid's own WebUI link is therefore http only. Do not port-forward this container directly. For remote access put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front (Pangolin, Traefik, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel...) that preserves the inbound Host header, add that hostname to DSH PUBLIC HOST, and have the proxy add HSTS and the usual security headers. In this image the Settings, Models and Credentials pages work through such a proxy; there is no need for an SSH tunnel.
SANDBOX: dsh runs untrusted commands confined to the Workspace path. The confinement uses Landlock, which is unprivileged and needs no extra capabilities, and if the kernel cannot enforce it dsh refuses to run rather than silently continuing unprotected. Keep the sandbox on unless your kernel lacks Landlock; the escape hatch is DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access, which lets the agent run commands with full access to this container's filesystem.
WHAT THE AGENT CAN REACH: the Workspace mount, and anything else you mount into it. Only mount data you are willing to let an AI read and modify.
VERSIONS: :latest follows the newest upstream release candidate (tracked from 0.2.0-rc.2 on). Every version we ship also gets its own tag (e.g. 0.2.0-rc.2) which you can pin in Repository instead. dsh is a developer preview with breaking changes between releases - 0.1.7 migrated session logs to a format that cannot be downgraded - so consider LEAVING AUTO-UPDATE OFF, backing up appdata first, and reading the release notes before updating.
IMAGE VARIANTS: the Repository above pulls the plain image. To change variant, edit Repository and Update. "-plus" adds a real system Chrome at /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable for plugins that drive a browser (dsh-realbrowser), python3/pip, the rtk command filter, the codebase-memory-mcp binary behind the code intelligence MCP server, and an Android reverse-engineering toolchain (jadx, apktool, smali/baksmali, aapt, dexdump, apksigner, zipalign, androguard) - roughly 1 GB more, most of it Chrome, one Java runtime shared by those tools, and the MCP server binary. Plus also installs opt-in CPU Selkies with authenticated Xvfb, PulseAudio and minimal Openbox, not a full desktop. Graphics is OFF by default; the container never launches Chrome itself. Before enabling, create an owned 0600 password file under Appdata and read docs/selkies.md for runtime/plugin ownership, hardened resource settings, local-only authenticated viewer access and pending verification. No graphics/CDP/X11 port is published. Existing disabled-mode behavior stays unchanged.
UPGRADING FROM ANOTHER IMAGE: point this template at a fresh appdata path first. The container entrypoint must own the state directory, and session logs from a 0.1.5 or older deployment are upgraded irreversibly on first start of 0.1.7.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: The dsh web interface. Reachable by anything that can route to this Unraid box, so treat the port as trusted-LAN only. Change the host port only if 3080 is taken.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Persistent dsh state: settings, API credentials, sessions, plugin installs. Ownership is adjusted automatically at startup, so no chown is needed. Back this up before every update.

Config.Name: Workspace
Config.Description: The directory the agent works in and the only place the sandbox lets it write. Point it at your projects if you prefer, but only mount data you are willing to let an AI modify. Existing files keep their ownership; the mount point itself is made writable.

Config.Name: DSH Public Host
Config.Description: Optional. The exact hostname you type in the browser, if you use one (e.g. unraid.local, or your domain behind a reverse proxy). No http://, no port unless it is non-standard. Without it, browsing by IP still works but a hostname gives HTTP 403. Added to the app as --trusted-host, and used for the login URL printed in the log.

Config.Name: Extra Trusted Hosts
Config.Description: Optional. More hostnames to accept, comma-separated, when you reach this container by several names (e.g. unraid.local,192.168.1.10:3080). Each becomes its own --trusted-host. Non-internal IP addresses need no entry here.

Config.Name: DeepSeek API Key
Config.Description: Optional. Your DeepSeek API key (sk-...). dsh reads it from the environment, so setting it here signs you in on first start; you can also add it later in the Models page instead, which stores it in appdata rather than in this container's configuration.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id dsh runs as, and the owner applied to Appdata at startup. 99 is Unraid's nobody, which is what your other appdata directories use. Set 1000 if you keep appdata owned by a normal user instead.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id dsh runs as. 100 is Unraid's users group. Pair with PUID: use 99:100 for nobody:users appdata, or 1000:1000 for a normal user.

Config.Name: Sandbox Mode
Config.Description: workspace-write (default) confines the agent to the Workspace path. read-only forbids writes there too. danger-full-access disables the sandbox entirely, giving the agent full access to this container's filesystem - only use it if your kernel cannot enforce Landlock and dsh refuses to start.

Config.Name: Graphics Enabled (Plus only)
Config.Description: Opt-in Selkies/Xvfb/PulseAudio. Requires Plus and an owned password file; no Chrome autolaunch or viewer port publication. See docs/selkies.md before enabling.

Config.Name: Graphics Display
Config.Description: Local X11 display number; do not reuse another owner's display.

Config.Name: Graphics Resolution
Config.Description: Initial WIDTHxHEIGHT; width multiple of 8, height even; within 3840x2160 ceiling.

Config.Name: Graphics Internal Port
Config.Description: Authenticated loopback-only Selkies port, not a host publication; must differ from DSH port.

Config.Name: Graphics Password File
Config.Description: Container path to single-line random password (12+ characters). Create in Appdata, mode 0600 owned by PUID:PGID, before enabling; do not put password in argv.
